sections.title: ShadowFormer: Global Context Helps Image Shadow Removal
sections.content_md:
ShadowFormer: Global Context Helps Image Shadow Removal

Lanqing Guo 1

sections.title: Problem
sections.content_md: Existing deep shadow removal methods often suffer from severe artifacts around shadow boundaries and inconsistent illumination because they focus locally and ignore the global contextual correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions.

sections.title: Core Idea
sections.content_md: ShadowFormer is a transformer-based network derived from a Retinex-based shadow model, designed to restore shadow-free images by leveraging global context. It employs a multi-scale encoder-decoder architecture using Channel Attention (CA) modules to efficiently capture hierarchical information. At the bottleneck stage, a Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM) utilizes Shadow-Interaction Attention (SIA) to model the correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions, allowing uncorrupted non-shadow areas to guide the restoration of shadowed areas for better illumination consistency and boundary artifact reduction.

sections.content_md: We introduce a Retinex-based shadow model that formulates the degradation and motivates exploiting global contexts for shadow removal.

sections.title: Method
sections.content_md:
ShadowFormer is a transformer-based network derived from a Retinex-based shadow model, designed to restore shadow-free images by leveraging global context. It employs a multi-scale encoder-decoder architecture using Channel Attention (CA) modules to efficiently capture hierarchical information. At the bottleneck stage, a Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM) utilizes Shadow-Interaction Attention (SIA) to model the correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions, allowing uncorrupted non-shadow areas to guide the restoration of shadowed areas for better illumination consistency and boundary artifact reduction.

**Key Formulas:**
- $$ \mathbf{I}_{s} = \mathbf{I}_m \odot \mathbf{L}_{s} \odot \mathbf{R} + (1-\mathbf{I}_m) \odot \mathbf{L}_{ns} \odot \mathbf{R} $$
  The Retinex-based shadow model decomposing the shadow image into shadow/non-shadow regions based on illumination and reflectance.
- $$ \mathbf{I}_{s}= \mathbf{I}_m \odot \mathbf{I}_{s} + (1-\mathbf{I}_m) \odot \mathbf{I}_{ns} $$
  The basic decomposition of a shadow image into shadow and non-shadow regions using a mask.
- $$ \text{SIA}(\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{\Sigma}) = \text{softmax}(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^T}{d})\mathbf{V} $$
  The core attention mechanism in the Shadow-Interaction Module, modified by correlation maps to emphasize context between shadow and non-shadow patches.
- $$ \tilde{\mathbf{X}}= \text{SIA}(\text{CA}(\text{LN}(\mathbf{X})),\mathbf{\Sigma})+ \mathbf{X} $$
  The residual connection formulation within the Shadow-Interaction Module combining Channel Attention and SIA.

sections.title: Results
sections.content_md:
| **Metric** | **Value** |
|-----------|----------|
| Datasets | ISTD, ISTD+, SRD |
| Metrics | PSNR, SSIM, Model Parameters, FLOPs |
| Best Result | ShadowFormer achieves state-of-the-art performance on all three datasets while using 5x to 150x fewer model parameters than competing methods. |

**Takeaways:**
- The proposed method effectively addresses boundary artifacts and illumination inconsistency by leveraging global context from non-shadow regions
- proving that transformer-based architectures with specific interaction modules are highly efficient for partial corruption tasks like shadow removal.

sections.title: Contributions
sections.content_md:
- **[theory]** We introduce a Retinex-based shadow model that formulates the degradation and motivates exploiting global contexts for shadow removal.
- **[method]** We propose ShadowFormer, a lightweight single-stage transformer network built on a multi-scale channel attention framework for end-to-end shadow removal.
- **[method]** We design a Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM) with Shadow-Interaction Attention (SIA) in the bottleneck stage to exploit global contextual correlations between shadow and non-shadow regions across spatial and channel dimensions.
- **[application]** We achieve state-of-the-art performance on ISTD, ISTD+, and SRD datasets using up to 150x fewer model parameters compared to existing methods.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content_md:
1. We introduce a Retinex-based shadow model that formulates the degradation and motivates exploiting global contexts for shadow removal.
2. We propose ShadowFormer, a lightweight single-stage transformer network built on a multi-scale channel attention framework for end-to-end shadow removal.
3. We design a Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM) with Shadow-Interaction Attention (SIA) in the bottleneck stage to exploit global contextual correlations between shadow and non-shadow regions across spatial and channel dimensions.
4. The proposed method effectively addresses boundary artifacts and illumination inconsistency by leveraging global context from non-shadow regions
5. proving that transformer-based architectures with specific interaction modules are highly efficient for partial corruption tasks like shadow removal.
